title: Examine the relationship between expertise, performance, and gaze behavior
author: Stephanie Brams1
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sk3ecyn

steps.title: Record baseline RPE score
steps.instruction: Have the participant rate his or her perceived exertion on the Borg RPE scale before beginning the first‑day error‑detection task.

steps.title: Provide error‑detection task instructions
steps.instruction: Explain that the participant will watch cockpit video clips, click with the mouse on any instrument that shows an error, otherwise make no click; after each clip answer the multiple‑choice question “I did not click because” with the options: non‑applicable (if a click was made), no error (if the cockpit functioned correctly), too late, or I have no idea. If the answer is “too late,” the researcher records the verbal response.

steps.title: Seat participant at eye‑tracker
steps.instruction: Position the participant in front of the Tobii T120 eye‑tracker at an approximate distance of 60 cm.

steps.title: Show cockpit instruction video
steps.instruction: Play the 10‑minute instruction video that gives a detailed explanation of the different cockpit instruments.

steps.title: Calibrate eye‑tracker and limit head movement
steps.instruction: Perform eye‑tracker calibration and instruct the participant to keep head movements to an absolute minimum during the experiment.

steps.title: Present 16 cockpit video clips
steps.instruction: Display the 16 video clips (recorded during the day) in which occasionally one instrument stops working; the participant clicks on the failing instrument if observed, otherwise makes no click, and then answers the multiple‑choice question as described.

steps.title: Record post‑task RPE score
steps.instruction: At the end of the first day, have the participant rate perceived exertion again on the Borg RPE scale.

steps.title: Conduct coherent motion task
steps.instruction: Run the coherent motion experiment consisting of a practice block followed by experimental trials.

substeps.instruction: Provide instructions: detect the direction of coherent moving dots among 600 random dots and indicate the direction using the keyboard.
Run 25 practice trials; a fixation cross in the centre provides feedback (green = correct, red = incorrect).

steps.title: Conduct Navon level‑switching task
steps.instruction: Run the Navon level‑switching experiment consisting of practice and test blocks.

substeps.instruction: Provide instructions: a white global figure composed of smaller local figures appears on a black background; detect squares or circles at either the global or local level, pressing F for a square and J for a circle as quickly and accurately as possible.
